messages:
maria: quick q — I'm writing a small wrapper to switch CLI profiles for CI jobs. what's the team's recommendation for storing/redwood auth tokens in CI? ENV var vs config file on disk? need noninteractive flow for ephemeral runners.

oliver: For CI we prefer short-lived tokens injected as env vars (REDWOOD_TOKEN). Simpler and avoids file-permission issues. Use a token exchange endpoint in your infra to mint one per job. If you have multiple profiles, set REDWOOD_PROFILE or pass --profile.

raj: If you must write a file (sidecar/container pattern), do an atomic write + strict perms to avoid races/peeks. Example:

```bash
# write token atomically and export for subprocesses
TMP=$(mktemp)
echo "$TOKEN" > "$TMP"
chmod 600 "$TMP"
mv "$TMP" ~/.redwood/ci-token
export REDWOOD_TOKEN_FILE=~/.redwood/ci-token
# consumer: redwood --token-file "$REDWOOD_TOKEN_FILE" ...
```

Also use unique filenames per job (e.g. add $CI_JOB_ID) to avoid parallel collisions.

sara: Another option is to surface secrets from your secret manager (Vault/GCP Secret Manager) at runtime and not persist them. We have an exchange endpoint that returns JSON: `{\"token\":\"...\",\"expires_at\":\"...\"}`. Example injector:

```bash
resp=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" https://infra.internal/v1/redwood/exchange?job=$CI_JOB_ID)
TOKEN=$(echo "$resp" | jq -r .token)
export REDWOOD_TOKEN="$TOKEN"
```

If you need to support long-running jobs, poll for renewal before expiry.

oliver: FYI streaming quirk — when running `redwood stream` inside non-interactive containers, make sure the CLI is launched without pseudo-tty/with the right flags. Otherwise chunked streaming can buffer. Use `--no-tty` or `REDWOOD_STREAM_MODE=lines`. Also consider `stdbuf -oL` if you pipe output in shell scripts.

maria: amazing, thanks. quick follow-up: do we have any shared helper scripts so I don't reinvent login_noninteractive? @devex-bot any pointers? :thinking: 

devex-bot: Heads-up — shared helpers live in `infra/ci/redwood_helpers.sh`. It includes `login_noninteractive`, `switch_profile_safe`, and `emit_token_json`. Link: https://git.internal/infra/infra/ci/redwood_helpers.sh (internal). :link: 

raj: One more gotcha — k8s secret mounts default to 0644 in some clusters; make sure the mount mode is 0400 and prefer tmpfs for secrets if possible. And for parallel runners, suffix profile names with job id: `redwood profile create ci-$CI_JOB_ID --token $TOKEN` then `redwood --profile ci-$CI_JOB_ID ...` so you avoid clobbering a shared config.

sara: :thumbsup: that pattern worked well for our e2e suite. ping me if you'd like pair on the exchange flow.

maria: will do — I'll try env-injection first and fall back to the atomic file approach if a helper process needs it. thanks all!
